_comment: Copy to oauth.json (gitignored) and build with: flutter build macos --dart-define-from-file=oauth.json
_google: Google Cloud console > Credentials > OAuth client ID > type 'Desktop app'. Desktop clients accept loopback on any port, so there is no redirect URI to register; a 'Web application' client instead needs http://127.0.0.1:53682 added explicitly. Both the id and the secret are required at the token endpoint: Google's 'client_secret not applicable' exemption covers only Android, iOS and Chrome clients. The secret is not confidential for installed apps and PKCE is what binds the exchange to this app.
_notion: Notion integrations > Public integration. Register http://localhost:53682 as the only redirect URI, spelled exactly so: Notion matches it verbatim and rejects redirect URIs written as an IP address. Notion supports no PKCE and authenticates the token exchange with HTTP Basic client_id:client_secret, so the secret cannot ship inside the app. Point NOTION_TOKEN_PROXY at a small endpoint you host that holds the secret, accepts {code, redirect_uri} as JSON and returns Notion's token response verbatim, passing redirect_uri through unchanged.
_notion_dev_only: Local development shortcut. Never set this in a build you distribute: anything in the binary can be extracted.
_deepseek: platform.deepseek.com > API keys. Used once per scan to file what was found into folders and categories; a build without it still scans and browses, and the Files section says the key is missing. Server keys are confidential, so a distributed build should call a proxy you host rather than carrying this.
